Series::round¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::round() const -> Series
Series& Series::round_()

What It Does¶

round() maps each lane to the nearest integer.

The most important behavior to know is the tie rule. On the current verified surface, half-way values round away from zero:

  • 1.5 -> 2

  • -1.5 -> -2

That tie rule affects the values you see and also tells you where the method’s discontinuity points matter most.

Returns¶

Series A new Series with nearest-integer rounded values.

Gradient¶

Between tie and integer boundaries, round() is locally constant, so the usual reverse-mode sensitivity is 0 through those lanes.

In-Place Form¶

round_() is the in-place sibling of round(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.4, 1.5, 2.5});

auto& ref = x.round_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 2]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. The current tie rule is half away from zero.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({-1.6, -1.5, -1.4, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6}).round();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[-2, -2, -1, 1, 2, 2]

Example 2. Reverse-mode sensitivity is zero in the ordinary piecewise-constant regions.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.2, 0.0, 3.8});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto y = x.round();
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "out=" << y << "\n";
std::cout << "dL_dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

out=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, 0, 4]
dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 0]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • round() is not the same as floor(), ceil(), or trunc().

  • Half-way cases matter; the current verified tie rule is away from zero.

  • The transform is not smooth.

Summary¶

Use round() when values should go to the nearest integer and the away-from-zero tie rule is acceptable for your policy.

See Also¶

  • Series::floor: always downward.

  • Series::ceil: always upward.

  • Series::trunc: toward-zero removal of the fractional part.
